Use only when the user explicitly asks to change the instruction system. Maintainer overview: `.claude/MAP.md`.

## Static frontend container

When the frontend is deployed as static assets, build it in a Node stage and serve the output with the selected hosting strategy (a web server image is not mandatory when the platform hosts static files). Keep API base URLs and environment configuration compatible with that strategy.

## .dockerignore

Exclude `.git`, `.vs`, `**/bin`, `**/obj`, `**/node_modules`, `TestResults`, `coverage`; do not exclude tests the image build intentionally runs or files restore/build needs.

## Image optimization

Start with standard supported images. Consider Alpine, chiseled images, trimming, or Native AOT only when compatibility and deployment requirements justify them, and verify globalization, native dependencies, reflection, and diagnostics when you do.

## Migrations and seeding

Container deployment does not change the production migration or Development-only seeding policies (`delivery-change`, `.claude/rules/backend/persistence.md`).

Build the image, verify application startup, required port/configuration, non-root behavior when relevant, health-probe integration, and the absence of accidental secrets/files; run meaningful tests outside or as part of the pipeline.

"Smoke test" means a small set of fast checks that a built or deployed application is basically operational — not a synonym for every integration test. Coverage is diagnostic, not a target; prioritize meaningful behavior, edge cases, and risky integrations. Snapshot testing can help for large stable outputs, but do not add a snapshot library by default; explicit assertions are clearer for small or important contracts.

## 3. Run relevant tests

Run tests covering the changed area (`dotnet test`, targeted where useful; the frontend's declared test script when one exists — inspect `package.json` rather than assuming a runner). Small solutions: run the full suite. Large solutions: affected test projects first, then the broader suite required by the repository or the change risk. Investigate every newly failing relevant test; never dismiss a failure as unrelated without checking it.

### Runtime smoke check

Default: for a new runnable application or substantial composition, startup, configuration, persistence, or full-stack changes, verify that the intended Development configuration actually starts, as applicable: the API host starts; the Development endpoint is reachable; Swagger UI loads when the API exposes it; required configuration binds; database connectivity and initialization succeed; the frontend dev server starts; the frontend API base URL and backend CORS configuration are compatible. A successful build alone does not prove runtime composition.

Review transaction/commit behavior, destructive data changes, raw SQL parameterization, authorization, input trust boundaries, secrets, sensitive logging, concurrency, migrations, and cache consistency. Run the full `security-scan` procedure only when a security audit was requested, the change is materially security-sensitive, or a concrete finding justifies broader investigation — not for every ordinary review.

- Frontend CI must use scripts that actually exist in the workspace's `package.json` and must use `npm ci` when a maintained lockfile supports it; never invent npm scripts and never reflexively replace a lockfile-based install with `npm install`.
- Enforced formatting/analyzer gates only when the project has adopted them; dependency vulnerability inspection per the project's security policy; no automatic package upgrades unless the project adopted automated updates.
- Integration-test infrastructure: per `ci-cd` (Integration-test infrastructure).

Expose liveness/readiness through ASP.NET Core health checks (`health-check`) and prefer orchestrator-native HTTP probes. Runtime images may lack `curl`, `wget`, or a shell; if Compose must run an in-container health command, verify the executable exists or add an explicit probe mechanism, weighing the cost of extra packages in production images.

## Static frontend container

When the frontend is deployed as static assets, build it in a Node stage and serve the output with the selected hosting strategy (a web server image is not mandatory when the platform hosts static files). Keep API base URLs and environment configuration compatible with that strategy.

## .dockerignore

Exclude `.git`, `.vs`, `**/bin`, `**/obj`, `**/node_modules`, `TestResults`, `coverage`; do not exclude tests the image build intentionally runs or files restore/build needs.

## Image optimization

Start with standard supported images. Consider Alpine, chiseled images, trimming, or Native AOT only when compatibility and deployment requirements justify them, and verify globalization, native dependencies, reflection, and diagnostics when you do.

## Migrations and seeding

Container deployment does not change the production migration or Development-only seeding policies (`delivery-change`, `.claude/rules/backend/persistence.md`).

## Verification

Build the image, verify application startup, required port/configuration, non-root behavior when relevant, health-probe integration, and the absence of accidental secrets/files; run meaningful tests outside or as part of the pipeline.
